headline: Strong sales beat drives earnings surge, guidance raised
summary_short: Ross Stores' fiscal Q1 2026 (13 weeks ended May 2, 2026) sales rose 21% to $6.01B on comparable store sales up 17%, with operating margin of 13.4% well above the company's own 11.8%-12.1% plan. Diluted EPS grew 37% to $2.02.
summary_long: Customer traffic drove the outperformance, with the company citing a successful Spring assortment transition, marketing-driven customer acquisition, an improved in-store experience, and a tailwind from tax-refund-related consumer spending. Operating margin of 13.4% beat the company's guided 11.8%-12.1% plan almost entirely on the sales beat. Diluted EPS (+37.4%) outpaced net income growth (+35.6%) as diluted share count fell ~1.8% y/y on buybacks ($319M repurchased this quarter under the $2.55B two-year authorization). The company issued initial Q2 FY2026 guidance (comp sales +6% to +7%, diluted EPS $1.85-$1.93) and raised full-year FY2026 guidance to comp sales +6% to +7% and diluted EPS $7.50-$7.74 (from an unstated prior range), citing continued strong underlying business fundamentals. Cash and equivalents were $4.13B at quarter-end.

drivers.explanation: Comparable store sales rose 17% on customer traffic, cited by the company as the primary driver, aided by merchandise assortment and marketing initiatives and a tax-refund spending tailwind.
13.4% margin came in well above the company's own 11.8%-12.1% plan, which management attributes primarily to the sales outperformance.
EPS growth (+37.4%) outpaced net income growth (+35.6%) because diluted weighted-average shares fell ~1.8% y/y from share buybacks.
CEO cites superb execution transitioning the Spring assortment and broad-based strength across the business as the quarter's narrative driver.
